title: Credit Control Note on the Number of Agreements One Customer May Hold Open — Belrose Layaway and Hold Agreements
content:
# Credit control note — agreements held open by one customer under Belrose Layaway and Hold Agreements

1. Each plan of Belrose Layaway and Hold Agreements caps how many of its own agreements one customer may hold open at a time; the cap is that plan's figure for the most agreements of the plan one customer may hold open at once. Taken across all the plans together, one customer holds no more than 4 agreements open at once.
2. An agreement counts as open while it stands at opened, current, delinquent or on hold. An agreement that has completed, forfeited or been cancelled no longer counts.
3. A further agreement is opened for a customer only when no agreement already recorded against the same agreement reference stands at opened, current, delinquent or on hold.
4. Whether an agreement stands open is read from the agreement record as it stands before the further agreement is opened, matched on the agreement reference; the customer's own account of which agreements are still running does not decide the point.
5. A customer at the cap may open another once one of theirs closes.

## Which states count toward the cap

| Standing of the agreement | Counts as open |
|---|---|
| opened | yes |
| current | yes |
| delinquent | yes |
| on hold | yes |
| completed | no |
| forfeited | no |
| cancelled | no |

## Two hypothetical positions on one plan

Both cases take a plan whose cap is, hypothetically, two agreements of that plan per customer.

- A customer holds one agreement of the plan at completed and one at delinquent. The completed agreement no longer counts; the delinquent one does. One agreement of the plan stands open, so the customer is below the plan's cap, and a further agreement may be opened for them provided no agreement recorded against the same agreement reference stands at opened, current, delinquent or on hold.
- The same customer holds one agreement of the plan at current and one at on hold. Both count, two agreements of the plan stand open, the customer is at the cap, and no further agreement of the plan is opened for them until one of the two closes.
